title: Camera exposure, localization calibration, and finite-time response bounds
status: Development specification fixed after analytic measurement-operator derivation and primary-source reading, before this lab's stochastic run. Previously studied thermal aliases are deliberate development cases, not held-out alternatives. No novelty or experimental-validation claim.

camera.operator: Two rectangular position averages on [0,h] and [T,T+h], not two instantaneous positions or integrated-velocity readings. Independent trajectories supply independent endpoint differences.
camera.noise_scope: Illustrative declared variance law, not a measured device or a universal photon model. Gaussian additive signal-independent per-frame errors. Calibration consists of independent immobile endpoint pairs at the same lag and exposure.

design.cost_scope: Every trajectory pair and every calibration pair costs two scalar position readings. Methods use identical sufficient statistics and counts. Exposure-integrated acquisition B*h and sequential pair-window proxy (B/2)*(T+h) are also reported, not equalized across exposures. No equal-cost comparison with velocity/acceleration hardware, no optimum shutter selection.

confidence.degrees_of_freedom: M-1 and L-1: centered Gaussian sample variances with unknown constant means
confidence.coverage: At least 95% for each prechosen cell and horizon under its assumptions; not a simultaneous family guarantee or post-selection guarantee.

method_formulas.signal_variance: [max(0,Lobs-(1+delta)*Ucal), Uobs-(1-delta)*Lcal]; negative upper endpoint means incompatible confidence constraints and is withheld, not projected to a false [0,0] claim
method_formulas.response: [Lsignal/2, min(T*T*C0/2, Usignal/2+C0*h*h/6, T*sqrt(C0*Usignal)/2)]; the last bound applies because T/h is an integer in every design. Empty intersection is withheld
method_formulas.transfer: delta=0 for strict transfer, delta=0.2 for bounded transfer. A variance ratio of 1.5 violates both transfer assumptions. The ignore-blur method omits both blur corrections and is deliberately invalid for the general camera model.

pre_stochastic_addition: Independent analytic review before implementation/run added J <= T*sqrt(C0*Jbar/2) for integer T/h, plus the sharp T=h special case. No simulation results were used to select it. Both additive and conditional bounds are retained in the blur-aware methods.
simulation: Exact independent chi-square sufficient statistics for centered Gaussian sample variances; not time-discretized paths. Persist every observed and calibration sum of squared deviations, intervals, compatibility flags, and confidence-event flags.
validation: Thermal matrices versus oscillatory VACF integrals
Camera time convolution versus independent frequency integration and refinement
Analytic universal blur bound plus discrete-spectrum stress checks
Gaussian common confidence event and deterministic interval coverage on that event
Equal reading accounting and full cell accounting
Noise telescoping for adjacent position differences
No-blur, ballistic, and Brownian limiting checks
decision_rule: No pass/fail performance gate and no post-run tuning. Report all exposures, both budgets, all drift conditions and each method, including undercoverage, broad bounds, and incompatible draws. Monte Carlo coverage is descriptive; the analytic confidence event is the guarantee.
limits: Synthetic stationary Gaussian thermal systems only; no camera images or apparatus validation.
Known finite velocity variance is essential; ideal overdamped Brownian velocity is not in this class.
Finite-time displacement is measured over the recorded horizon, not forecast beyond the record.
Interpreting passive MSD as forced response needs equilibrium fluctuation-dissipation and linear response.
Independent trajectory ensembles are not replaced by overlapping increments from one movie.
Signal-dependent localization, non-Gaussian errors, shutter uncertainty, interparticle dependence, and calibration drift outside the declared range are not covered.
A narrower absolute interval need not be a useful relative interval for a very small response.
